item.text:
**No-go until the design distinguishes a production question from a missing clean-system row.** Version 2 resolves the composite objection: it keeps new-system events and undirected themes out of the calculation, names the affected driver and does not renormalise the weights. It also covers two-choice events and the server-side planner. [DESIGN.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/DESIGN.md:16)

The remaining problem is the table’s last row: **“No row (production’s ledgers) → unchanged.”** The preceding display contract deliberately permits a `clean_ladders` table with no row for a view, including a question written by another writer. In that case both proposed shape fields are `None`; no row does not establish that the question is production’s. Falling back to the old score inference could therefore invent a direction on an unidentified question—the precise outcome this slice is intended to prevent. [Display design](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/not-judged-display/DESIGN.md:14), [page contract](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/DESIGN.md:21)

Specify a source or compatibility discriminator that distinguishes a known production ledger from an unknown or missing row. For the unknown case, preserve the stored labels and make a direction-dependent composite unavailable, or refuse with a clear reason; test a mixed store and before-creation suppression. Once that contract is written, the standalone lane and neutral-tone design is suitable to build and prove.

CONSENSUS: no, because a missing ladder row is currently treated as proof of a production question and can trigger an invented score.
